page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the Nitro virtualization architecture. It is powered by 32 physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton (Neoverse-N1) processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, provisioned as 32 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core. The instance provides 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a substantial 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage consists of a local 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. It contains no hardware GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects solid multi-threaded performance and caching behavior alongside predictable single-thread limitations characteristic of the ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture. In multi-core throughput, the server achieved a stress-ng score of 48,566.12 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 11,488.0, both within average ranges. Cached memory bandwidth reached 1894.65 GB/sec for small 16 KB read blocks, settling into 139.81 GB/sec for large 256 MB uncached reads and 70.12 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-thread metrics skew lower, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 942.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression of 7.26 GB/sec.

The 1:16 core-to-memory configuration delivers high resource density for workloads bottlenecked on memory capacity rather than raw IPC. While lack of AVX/AMX instruction sets and modest single-core speeds reduce its efficiency for compute-heavy vector processing or low-latency generation pipelines, it demonstrates reliable operational throughput for in-memory systems, reaching 36.44 million Redis SET operations per second and 20,286.9 in PassMark database tests.

Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is best suited for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-volume key-value stores, real-time analytics engines, and big data processing pipelines that require generous memory capacity paired with high-speed local NVMe scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores using AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of memory (16.0 GB per vCPU), a 1900 GB local NVMe SSD, and 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without dedicated GPUs. In benchmarks, the instance yields average multi-core CPU capacity (11,488.0 Geekbench multi-core, 48,566.12 stress-ng) and strong cached memory bandwidth, though single-core compute performance remains in the lower percentiles. Delivering 36.44 million Redis SET operations per second and over 20,000 on PassMark database tests, this server offers efficient resource density for memory-bound tasks. It is ideally matched for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale data ingestion, and memory-intensive analytics workloads requiring fast local scratch disks.
